author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected through a form prefilled with its current values. The correction updates that visit in place, never adds a second visit, and is held to the same rules as a booking.
acceptance_criteria: given a booked visit, when its correction form opens, then the form shows that visit's current date and description
given a booked visit, when a description and a date later than today are submitted, then that visit is updated in place and the owner's record is shown
given a booked visit, when a correction is accepted, then the pet has the same number of visits as before
given a blank description, when a correction is submitted, then the correction is refused, the form is shown again, and the description is named
given a date of today or earlier, when a correction is submitted, then the correction is refused, the form is shown again, and the date is named
edge case 3: correcting a visit that is not recorded against the named pet is refused, and no visit changes
edge case 4: correcting a visit for a pet that does not belong to the named owner is refused, and no visit changes
non_goals: any link or button into the correction from the owner's record or any other page (owner decision: reachable by its URL alone; a visible entry point may come as a follow-up request)
moving a visit to a different pet
a confirmation message after an accepted correction
correcting a past visit without moving its date past today
notes: Request surface quoted at intake line 1: GET and POST on /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit, reusing the existing visit form template and its `visit` model attribute; success redirects to the owner detail page. Edited docs this dispatch: docs/prd.md (NG-5 row narrowed, Non-Goals preamble, REQ-VIS-003 narrative, 5 Done-when bullets, edge cases 3-5, ADR link, 2 open questions), new docs/adr/2026-09-30-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md, status line of docs/adr/2026-08-08-non-goal-deletion-and-visit-amendment.md. Outside my write scope: docs/adr/README.md index needs a row for the 2026-09-30 non-goal ADR. Narrowest-reading decisions (reversible, no owner answer available): a visit id not recorded against the named pet, or a pet not owned by the named owner, is refused (edge cases 3-4); no confirmation message is added, so no new wording is required under REQ-LANG-002; past-dated visits follow the quoted rule literally (date must be later than today) -- recorded as a PRD open question. Open, not decided: the reused form's submit button reads 'Add Visit' on a correction; the intake mandates template reuse and says nothing on wording, so this slice requires no wording change. test_names: the two refusal cases per data-driven test are one behavior each (blank description / non-future date; foreign visit / foreign pet).

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Visit correction extends VisitController with GET/POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit, following the aggregate rule in system-design.md § Contracts (new 'Visit correction' invariant): the visit is reached Owner -> Pet -> Visit by identity and saved through OwnerRepository by cascade, with no new repository. The existing patterns cover the rest. The PetController.findPet precedent, an optional path variable on the model-attribute method, resolves an existing visit versus a new one. Owner.getPet(Integer) is the model for a Pet lookup of a visit by identity. The booking handler's non-future-date check and its owner redirect are reused. Adjustments are small: a Pet visit-by-identity lookup, an allow-list on the visit binder, and a new § Scale and Load row. The existing template is reused unchanged: it posts to the current URL, and its heading already drops 'New' for a persisted visit. The success path adds no flash message, which the PRD lists as a non-goal. Basis: grep and read of VisitController, PetController, Owner, Pet, Visit and the template; the IDE oracle is not connected.
integration_points: Double, repository boundary (OwnerRepository): reuse VisitControllerTests' existing class-level @MockitoBean OwnerRepository stub. findById returns a real Owner -> Pet -> Visit graph whose visit carries an id. Assertions read that real graph and verify save / never save. Reason for the framework stub: the @WebMvcTest slice carries no JPA context, and OwnerRepository extends JpaRepository, too wide for a hand-written double. No other stub is sanctioned.
Double, framework transport: MockMvc (the sanctioned harness, testing-principles § Mocking Policy).

Binding, GET/POST .../visits/{visitId}/edit: the target is the persisted Visit resolved through the owner aggregate, behind a binder allow-list of the form's two fields (date, description). The existing id / *.id disallow list is kept (security-principles § Realization, mass assignment). No owner field is request-bound on this route. The allow-list sits on VisitController's binder, so booking binds the same two fields.

Model-attribute resolution: the 'visit' model-attribute method takes visitId as an optional path variable (PetController.findPet precedent). When it is present, the method returns the named pet's existing visit, found by identity, and adds nothing to the pet. When it is absent, today's new-visit-added-to-pet behavior is unchanged. A visitId absent from the pet throws IllegalArgumentException before binding, exactly as the unknown-pet case does, and carries only ids.

Success: owners.save(owner), then redirect to /owners/{ownerId}. Validation failure: return the form view before any save. The date check is the same one booking uses, with the same field and code (date, typeMismatch.visitDate).

patterns.description: optional path variable on the @ModelAttribute method separating create from edit
lookup by identity through the aggregate; mirror it on Pet for visits
non-future-date rejection, redisplay on errors, redirect to owner; extract the date check once so both handlers call it

risks.risk: Today's 'visit' model-attribute method adds a new Visit to the pet on every request. If it runs unchanged on the correction route, save cascades a second, blank visit. That breaks the Done-when rule that the pet keeps the same number of visits (system-design.md § Contracts, Visit correction invariant).
risks.mitigation: Branch on the optional visitId so the correction path never calls pet.addVisit. theVisitEditShouldNotAddAVisitToThePet asserts the pet's visit count is unchanged. It also asserts that the corrected instance is the one saved.

risks.risk: Copying the non-future-date check into the correction handler would give one rule two copies (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog, Web controller row and its note on controller-held rules).
risks.mitigation: Both handlers call one shared check in VisitController. The rule stays within the recorded deviation (system-design.md Open Question 2), and the correction adds no rule.

risks.risk: The controller's handler takes @ModelAttribute Owner, which is bound from the request, and the binder disallows only ids. Any Owner field submitted to the correction route (e.g. telephone) would bind, and save would persist it (security-principles § Realization, mass assignment; system-design.md § Threat Model, mass-assignment row).
risks.mitigation: Put an allow-list of date and description on the visit binder, keeping the id disallow list. Booking's binding narrows to the same two fields, and the form loses nothing. The correction success test adds one non-form parameter and asserts the owner is unchanged.

risks.risk: A foreign visit or pet reaching the correction route must be refused with no visit changed, and the error page renders exception messages (system-design.md § Known Defects, REQ-SYS-002; security-principles § Realization, secret disclosure).
risks.mitigation: Refuse in model-attribute resolution before binding, with an IllegalArgumentException carrying only ids. theVisitEditShouldRefuseAVisitOutsideTheNamedOwnerAndPet asserts the IllegalArgumentException cause, that save is never called, and that the visit's values are unchanged.

risks.risk: Resolving a visit by identity scans the pet's visit collection (system-design.md § Scale and Load, row 'One pet's visits').
risks.mitigation: Use the simplest readable form: a linear scan of the eagerly loaded collection, with no index or query.

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; skipped. Design-doc writes this dispatch: in docs/system-design.md, the 'Visit correction' invariant note under Contracts; REQ-VIS-003 added to the Owner, Pet, Visit, OwnerRepository and VisitController rows; and a new § Scale and Load section from the doctor template with one row. The Threat Model mass-assignment row now names the visit binder's allow-list. In docs/adr/README.md, the index row for 2026-09-30-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md that the product expert flagged, and the 2026-08-08 row's status noting the NG-5 amendment. No architectural ADR: the slice reuses recorded patterns and no decision constrains later slices. The PRD open questions (the reused 'Add Visit' button wording on a correction, past-dated visits, a visible entry link) need no design change and stay open for the owner. architecture-principles.md needs no edit: the non-future-date check stays in the controller under the existing, recorded deviation. Moving it to a Form validator is Open Question 2's resolution, not this slice's.

findings.description: docs/system-design.md:92 assigns Pet the rule 'finds one of them by identity', and line 130 names the linear scan of the visit collection. approved_aspects: Mass assignment: VisitController.setAllowedFields now calls dataBinder.setAllowedFields("date", "description") while keeping setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id"). An unnamed @InitBinder applies to every model attribute in the controller, so the Owner bound by @ModelAttribute on both POST routes now takes no fields at all. That closes owner-field tampering on the new edit route and on the existing booking route, and the test theVisitEditShouldUpdateTheVisitInPlaceAndShowTheOwnerRecord shows a tampered telephone is ignored. summary: add in-place correction of a booked visit

blast_radius.note: One module and two production files (82 lines): Pet gains a lookup by identity, and VisitController gains the two /visits/{visitId}/edit mappings. The binder allow-list also reaches the existing booking route, but it is deliberate hardening that the design-block names and the round-1 security reviewer verified. semantic_surprise.note: The core logic reads correctly: the Owner->Pet->Visit chain refuses foreign ids before binding, the non-future check is shared, and save runs only when there are no errors. The unchanged template carries surprises, though. The correction page's button still says 'Add Visit'. On a refused correction, the bound visit is the same instance held in pet.visits, so the Previous Visits table shows the rejected date and description as though they were recorded. Nothing is persisted. Separately, the allow-list silently stops the booking POST from binding the hidden petId and any Owner field.

test_adequacy.note: The tests are real. They check the prefilled values, the in-place update by recursive comparison, a tampered telephone being ignored, cross-pet and cross-owner refusals with no save, and PetTests reaches the isNew guard.
